parameters.query:
-- App-delete slot release (2026-08-27): retiring here, synchronously with the app's
-- delete action, is the ONLY coverage for status='active' owners -- Profile Lifecycle
-- Sweep's Branch B deliberately never touches them, and Count Channels would otherwise
-- hold the dead bot's slot forever (live incident: bot «16», profile dec53892-d97f).
-- Match by profile_id ONLY (the PK, sent by the app that owns it): scoping by
-- app_user_id would MISS rows created under a different identity (RevenueCat anonymous
-- id rotation / the pre-init deviceUniqueIdentifier fallback) -- appUserId in the body
-- is audit-only. The final SELECT guarantees exactly one output item so the chain can
-- never die on a zero-row update; '-1'/'' are the client's unauthed sentinels.
with retired as (
  update bot_profiles
     set deleted_at = now(), deleted_reason = 'app_delete'
   where deleted_at is null
     and profile_id in ($1, $2)
     and profile_id not in ('-1', '')
   returning profile_id
)
select count(*)::int as "retiredProfiles" from retired;

WITH matched AS (
  SELECT id, metadata->>'fileId' AS file_id
  FROM documents
  WHERE (metadata->>'botWaId' = $1 AND $1 NOT IN ('-1', ''))
     OR (metadata->>'botTgId' = $2 AND $2 NOT IN ('-1', ''))
),
deleted AS (
  DELETE FROM documents WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM matched) RETURNING id
)
SELECT
  (SELECT count(*)::int FROM deleted) AS "deletedChunks",
  COALESCE((SELECT array_agg(DISTINCT file_id) FROM matched WHERE file_id IS NOT NULL AND file_id <> ''), '{}'::text[]) AS "fileIds";

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { "success": true, "deletedChunks": $('Delete Bot Chunks').first().json.deletedChunks, "deletedFiles": ($('Delete Bot Chunks').first().json.fileIds || []).length, "retiredProfiles": $('Retire Bot Profiles').first().json.retiredProfiles ?? null, "deletedMemoryRows": $json.deletedMemoryRows ?? null, "deletedOutcomes": $json.deletedOutcomes ?? null, "deletedReplyFlags": $json.deletedReplyFlags ?? null, "deletedHistoryEvents": $json.deletedHistoryEvents ?? null, "deletedHandoffs": $json.deletedHandoffs ?? null, "deletedReplyEvents": $json.deletedReplyEvents ?? null, "deletedChatStates": $json.deletedChatStates ?? null } }}

parameters.query:
-- Privacy deletion (2026-09-01, store audit / Data Safety «можно запросить удаление»):
-- a deleted bot's server-side conversation memory goes with it. Chat transcripts key
-- off session_id = '<profileId>:<chatId>' (both bot templates' Chat Memory nodes),
-- conversation_outcomes and reply_mode_flags carry profile_id directly. Sentinels
-- '-1'/'' (channel never authed) are excluded like Delete Bot Chunks guards its ids;
-- 'null'/'undefined' cover a missing body field stringified by queryReplacement.
-- dialog_counts stay UNTOUCHED on purpose: they are the owner's billing usage records
-- (Task 17a moves them with the money on transfer), not chat content.
WITH ids AS (
  SELECT unnest(ARRAY[$1, $2]) AS profile_id
), valid AS (
  SELECT profile_id FROM ids
  WHERE profile_id IS NOT NULL AND profile_id NOT IN ('-1', '', 'null', 'undefined')
), hist AS (
  DELETE FROM public.n8n_chat_histories h
  WHERE split_part(h.session_id, ':', 1) IN (SELECT profile_id FROM valid)
  RETURNING 1
), outcomes AS (
  DELETE FROM public.conversation_outcomes c
  WHERE c.profile_id IN (SELECT profile_id FROM valid)
  RETURNING 1
), flags AS (
  DELETE FROM public.reply_mode_flags f
  WHERE f.profile_id IN (SELECT profile_id FROM valid)
  RETURNING 1
), hist_events AS (   -- stage 4: the one history
  DELETE FROM public.chat_history_events e
  WHERE e.profile_id IN (SELECT profile_id FROM valid)
  RETURNING 1
), handoffs AS (      -- stage 4: the bot's requests (and their pending notices)
  DELETE FROM public.handoff_requests r
  WHERE r.profile_id IN (SELECT profile_id FROM valid)
  RETURNING 1
), events AS (        -- stage 3: the event ledger + per-chat state
  DELETE FROM public.reply_events r
  WHERE r.profile_id IN (SELECT profile_id FROM valid)
  RETURNING 1
), states AS (
  DELETE FROM public.chat_reply_state s
  WHERE s.profile_id IN (SELECT profile_id FROM valid)
  RETURNING 1
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*)::int FROM hist)        AS "deletedMemoryRows",
       (SELECT count(*)::int FROM outcomes)    AS "deletedOutcomes",
       (SELECT count(*)::int FROM flags)       AS "deletedReplyFlags",
       (SELECT count(*)::int FROM hist_events) AS "deletedHistoryEvents",
       (SELECT count(*)::int FROM handoffs)    AS "deletedHandoffs",
       (SELECT count(*)::int FROM events)      AS "deletedReplyEvents",
       (SELECT count(*)::int FROM states)      AS "deletedChatStates";

-- V12: may this install delete these ids? Decided here, never from the token's lists (live rows only, up to 12 h
-- old). A session may delete when its install is not revoked and EVERY id the delete will use is a string that belongs
-- to a bot_profiles row whose owner is this install, retired or not (a workflow id: the row it is bound to). A row
-- without an owner (never claimed) is never proof; at least one real id must be named. A token-less legacy call keeps
-- the old behaviour while the compat window is open. Read-only. `reason` says why a refusal happened: owned_elsewhere
-- (another install owns one of the ids) or unproven. Parameters, in order: gate mode, install id, JSON array of the
-- profile ids, JSON array of the workflow ids.
with ids as (
  select 'p'::text as kind, v #>> '{}' as id, jsonb_typeof(v) as t from jsonb_array_elements($3::jsonb) v
  union all
  select 'w'::text, v #>> '{}', jsonb_typeof(v) from jsonb_array_elements($4::jsonb) v
), named as (
  select kind, id from ids where t = 'string' and id not in ('', '-1')
), verdict as (
  select case
    when $1 = 'legacy' then 'ok'
    when $1 is distinct from 'session' or coalesce($2, '') = '' then 'unproven'
    when not exists (select 1 from installs i where i.install_id = $2 and i.revoked_at is null) then 'unproven'
    when exists (select 1 from ids where t <> 'string') then 'unproven'
    when not exists (select 1 from named) then 'unproven'
    when not exists (select 1 from named n where not exists (
           select 1 from bot_profiles bp where bp.owner_id = $2
              and ((n.kind = 'p' and bp.profile_id = n.id) or (n.kind = 'w' and bp.workflow_id = n.id)))) then 'ok'
    when exists (select 1 from named n join bot_profiles bp
                   on (n.kind = 'p' and bp.profile_id = n.id) or (n.kind = 'w' and bp.workflow_id = n.id)
                 where bp.owner_id is not null and bp.owner_id <> $2) then 'owned_elsewhere'
    else 'unproven' end as v
)
select (v = 'ok') as allowed, case when v = 'ok' then null else v end as reason from verdict;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $json.crAuth.mode, ($json.crAuth.installId || ''), JSON.stringify([ ($json.body || {}).waProfileId ?? null, ($json.body || {}).tgProfileId ?? null ]), JSON.stringify([ ($json.body || {}).botWaId ?? null, ($json.body || {}).botTgId ?? null ]) ] }}

parameters.query:
-- V12: the deleted bot's stored price-list originals, listed BEFORE anything is deleted (the storage delete runs
-- first; a failure stops the chain with the chunks still in place, so the retry finds the same files). Read-only.
-- Parameters, in order: the bot's WhatsApp and Telegram workflow ids (the sentinels match nothing).
select coalesce(array_agg(distinct d.metadata->>'fileId') filter (where coalesce(d.metadata->>'fileId', '') <> ''), '{}'::text[]) as "fileIds"
from documents d
where (d.metadata->>'botWaId' = $1 and $1 not in ('-1', ''))
   or (d.metadata->>'botTgId' = $2 and $2 not in ('-1', ''));

conditions.leftValue: ={{ typeof $('Retire Bot Profiles').first().json.retiredProfiles === 'number' && typeof $('Delete Bot Chunks').first().json.deletedChunks === 'number' && typeof $json.deletedMemoryRows === 'number' && typeof $json.deletedOutcomes === 'number' && typeof $json.deletedReplyFlags === 'number' && typeof $json.deletedHistoryEvents === 'number' && typeof $json.deletedHandoffs === 'number' && typeof $json.deletedReplyEvents === 'number' && typeof $json.deletedChatStates === 'number' }}
